title: Integrated onboard scaffold for atomic profile transitions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a reusable CI/CD scaffold that performs atomic transitions of model versions + performance profiles with verifiable artifacts and a lightweight canary path. This ticket covers the pipeline definition, artifact hash locking, signing metadata emission, staged traffic handoff (ephemeral canary), and deterministic rollback mechanisms. Goal: replace the current multi-step manual publish where profiles and model pins are updated in separate systems, which can lead to mismatches and transient customer-facing regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Single pipeline job (release-bridge) takes a model bundle and performance profile and produces: signed bundle artifact, signed profile manifest, and a monotonic transition manifest containing previous and next pins.
2) Transition manifest is cryptographically verifiable (cosign signature + provenance hash) and contains TTL for canary phase and operator metadata.
3) Canary path: pipeline can apply a short-lived canary pin that redirects X% of traffic for N minutes, then either promote to full pin or revert automatically based on health checks.
4) Rollback: if promotion fails, the system reverts to previous pin and emits an incident event with trace links within 2 minutes of failure detection.
5) All artifacts and manifests are published to the model registry and a signed pointer is stored in release-broker; console UI shows the transition as an atomic operation (single audit event).
6) End-to-end integration tests that simulate a canonical canary-promote-revert sequence pass in CI and are part of the merge gating step.
7) Developers can run a local 'release-bridge --dry-run' that outputs the three artifacts and a deterministic signature that matches CI output.
8) Documentation: short runbook + design doc linked in the ticket and a Console change request is created for rollout day.
implementation_notes: We will implement a new GitHub Actions workflow (release-bridge.yml) that composes existing build steps (model bundle creation) with a new 'transition' step that writes the monotonic transition manifest.
Use cosign (SHA-256) for signing both the model bundle and profile manifest; signatures should be timestamped and include signer key id.
Transition manifest schema (flat JSON file) must include: previous_pin, candidate_pin, profile_ref, canary_percent, canary_duration_secs, promoted_by, timestamp, provenance_hash, and signature.
Introduce a short-lived 'canary pin' channel in release-broker: pins have a 'scope' field (global | canary) and an expiry timestamp to auto-revert if not promoted.
Health checks for canary promotion are a composite: latency SLA (p50/p95), error rate delta vs baseline, and a small set of smoke prompts evaluated by existing quality harness.
Telemetry: emit a unified transition.trace_id and wire to console's rollout dashboard; include tokenized links to the model registry entry and perf profile page.
Local dev helper: npm cli 'rw-release' (or go binary) that mirrors the GH Action steps using local docker image and writes artifacts into ./out for inspection.
Add integration tests in 'ci/integration/release-bridge' that run the full dry-run, signed manifest verification, and a simulated canary traffic flood using the workload generator.
Edge-case: support model bundles with identical content but different metadata; use content-addressable hash of the model artifact tarball to determine previous_pin equivalence.
risks: Key management: cosign private keys must be protected; initial approach uses ephemeral CI signing keys stored in vault with limited TTL — need approval from security for rotation policy.
Race conditions if multiple release-bridge jobs run concurrently for same model; must implement optimistic locking using registry sequence numbers or compare-and-swap semantics.
Canary window misconfiguration could cause false positives or unnecessary rollbacks; we need safe defaults and guardrails in the workflow config.
Operator confusion: new atomic transition hides multi-step internals; provide clear console explanations and an 'inspect' view showing signed artifacts.
